Bavarian Nordic Launches Next Tranche of DKK 750 Million Share Buy-Back Program
sum: КОПЕНГАГЕН, Дания, 13 ноября 2026 г. – Bavarian Nordic A/S (OMX: BAVA) сегодня запускает второй транш программы выкупа акций, объявленной 21 августа, в рамках которой компания намерена выкупить собственные акции на сумму до 750 миллионов датских крон. Второй транш будет включать выкуп акций на сумму до 250 миллионов датских крон.

Целью новой программы обратного выкупа акций является корректировка структуры капитала путем последующего аннулирования акций, выкупленных в рамках этой программы, с учетом любых необходимых дополнительных корпоративных решений, если это применимо.

Программа обратного выкупа акций инициируется в соответствии с разрешением, полученным на ежегодном общем собрании 21 апреля 2026 года, а также в соответствии с Регламентом (ЕС) № 596/2014 (с поправками) Европейского парламента и Совета о злоупотреблениях на рынке, а также Делегированным регламентом Комиссии (ЕС) 2016/1052, которые вместе составляют Регламент о безопасной гавани.

Bavarian Nordic назначила Danske Bank ведущим менеджером по осуществлению обратного выкупа акций в соответствии с условиями программы и с полномочиями принимать торговые решения самостоятельно и без влияния Bavarian Nordic.
- Программа обратного выкупа акций начнется 13 ноября 2026 г. и завершится не позднее 15 января 2027 г.
- Акции на общую сумму до 250 миллионов датских крон могут быть выкуплены.
- В течение срока действия программы будет выкуплено максимум 2 000 000 акций.

Hjarsø El-teknik ApS becomes part of InstallatørGruppen
sum: 12.11.2026 08:31:01 CET | GlobeNewswire by notified | Press release

InstallatørGruppen has entered into an agreement to acquire Hjarsø El-teknik ApS, an electrical installation company based in Greve, Denmark, serving private and commercial customers in the Greater Copenhagen area. The acquisition marks InstallatørGruppen's 44th acquisition in Denmark, bringing the total number of companies across Denmark and Switzerland to 50.

Including one previously announced transaction in Denmark, which is pending regulatory approval, the total number of acquisitions in Denmark will be 45, and the total number of companies across Denmark and Switzerland will increase to 51.

Hjarsø El-teknik was founded by Christian Hjarsø in 2016 and has since grown into a modern, service-oriented electrical contractor with 18 employees. The company carries out all types of electrical work, from service, electrical inspections and switchboard replacement to renovation and energy optimisation. In addition, Hjarsø El-teknik works with solar panels, EV charging stations, smart installations, AI and CTS.

The acquisition strengthens InstallatørGruppen's position within electrical installation in the western part of Copenhagen and the Greater Copenhagen area and adds a well-functioning service business with high customer satisfaction to the Group.
Hjarsø El-teknik will continue as an independently run company under its current management, consisting of Christian Hjarsø, in line with InstallatørGruppen's decentralised partnership model.

Peter Frandsen, Country CEO of InstallatørGruppen in Denmark, comments: “Christian Hjarsø has built a modern and well-run electrical company with a strong focus on service and quality – and that is something the customers notice. This is exactly the kind of professional pride and local roots we value in our companies. We look forward to welcoming Christian and his employees to the Group.”

sum: Deutsche Bank raised its price target for DSV A/S on October 22, 2026, while reiterating a Buy rating. The bank lifted the target from DKK 1,425 to DKK 1,680, an increase of 17.9 percent, according to MarketScreener.

Deutsche Bank's move therefore stood out as a more positive reassessment among the broker updates listed for October 22.

The target price is an analyst estimate rather than company guidance. Investors will therefore weigh the revised valuation against DSV's operating performance, the integration of acquired logistics activities and the range of views among covering banks.

DSV provides transportation services across air and sea freight, road transportation and logistics. Its logistics activities include storage, packaging, loading dock transfer and distribution services for industrial customers. MarketScreener classifies the company in the Air Freight & Logistics sector.

sum: 7.11.2026 13:55:57 CET | GlobeNewswire by notified | Press release

WUHU, China, Nov. 07, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- LUXEED staged its global brand launch on October 21 at Wuhu’s Shenshan Intelligent Valley, where flagship models LLounge and Stormax made their global debut. LUXEED Senior Designer Jonathan James Hodder and LUXEED International Vice‑President Danny Xia walked media through the brand’s defining design philosophy and underlying engineering framework.

Centered on TIANDIRENHE (Harmony of Heaven, Earth and Humanity), LUXEED’s global design philosophy merges aerodynamic form, engineering integrity and human‑centric driving pleasure. Four signature design aesthetics — Digital, Proportional, Sculptural and Performance‑oriented — underpin its ambition of “100 METERS, ONE GLANCE, RECOGNIZED.” LLounge features stately vertical L‑shaped headlamps for executive poise; Stormax sports horizontal dual‑L headlights and wind‑cut lines to amplify its sporty character. Cabin development follows four dimensions: Clear Architecture, Living Aura, Iconic Touch and Sculpted Support, with meticulous material selection and craftsmanship that follows the standard of “precise to the detail, refined to perfection.”

LUXEED’s intelligent driving technology is built on three pillars: one-stage end-to-end learning, reinforcement learning, and world models. Together, these technologies aim to move beyond simply perceiving the environment toward understanding and anticipating it. Inside the cabin, the 8397 intelligent chip, multimodal sensing architecture, and onboard AI model work together to recognize occupants’ states and their surroundings, enabling more proactive, responsive interactions.

The Vehicle Motion Control (VMC) system orchestrates core vehicle subsystems with sub‑1‑millisecond decision latency, paired with high‑spec chassis hardware including dual‑chamber air suspension and ±7° rear‑wheel steering. Even the 5.3‑metre‑plus LLounge delivers tight manoeuvrability with a 5.35‑metre turning radius. Luxury cabin amenities include one‑second adjustable-tint privacy glass and an immersive 33‑speaker audio system, while 2,400 MPa steel and the 3‑6‑0 comprehensive safety system provide an additional foundation for occupant protection.

items.t: DSV shares surge on third-quarter revenue beat, share buyback launch
sum: Investing.com -- DSV shares jumped nearly 8% in early Copenhagen trading Wednesday after the company reported better-than-expected third-quarter revenue and announced a 1.5 billion crown share buyback program, first since its acquisition of Schenker.
Third-quarter revenue came in at 80.7 billion Danish crowns, beating analyst estimates of 74.7 billion crowns and marking a 12% increase from a year earlier.
Adjusted net income rose to 4.07 billion crowns, surpassing the consensus estimate of 3.85 billion. However, adjusted EBIT of 6.61 billion crowns came in slightly below the estimate of 6.66 billion.

The Denmark-based transport and logistics firm narrowed its fiscal 2026 adjusted EBIT guidance to 24 billion to 25 billion crowns from a previous range of 23.5 billion to 25.5 billion. The midpoint of 24.5 billion sits above the analyst consensus of 24.41 billion. The company also reduced its expected special items for integration costs to 5.5 billion crowns from 6.5 billion.

Earnings growth was driven by strong results in the Air & Sea and Contract Logistics divisions, supported by cost synergies from the Schenker integration. The Road division saw earnings decline due to negative volume growth and lower productivity stemming from operational issues related to the Schenker integration. Property disposals also contributed to EBIT across all divisions.

The company noted that its demand outlook continues to be affected by rising energy prices and global inflation. DSV expects an effective tax rate of about 28% for 2026, citing the ongoing Schenker integration.

items.t: DSV (CPSE:DSV) Climbed, So What Is Behind The Latest Attention?
sum: DSV (CPSE:DSV) has agreed a logistics partnership with Skyways that brings autonomous aircraft into offshore energy supply routes, starting with North Sea operations from Norden, Germany, this fall.

For investors tracking DSV, the new Skyways deal lands after a mixed stretch in the market. The share price has climbed 3.41% over the last day but is down 9.27% over 30 days and 27.16% over 90 days, while the 1 year total shareholder return has declined 8.90%. This signals pressure on longer term sentiment even as short term momentum shows signs of stabilising around the recent DKK1,199 level. Operational developments such as the Porsche Carrera Cup logistics work and this autonomous aircraft move are reshaping how the business is being priced for risk and future demand.
Scan other logistics and infrastructure plays that could benefit from similar shifts toward automation by reviewing our curated list of 90 AI infrastructure stocks alongside DSV.
DSV now finds itself with a fresh automation story, a softer one year return and a DKK1,199 share price. Does that mix still leave more upside for new buyers than downside if things disappoint?

On the most followed view, DSV is priced at a clear markdown. The narrative fair value of DKK2,194 sits well above the recent DKK1,199 close, which puts fresh weight on how long term holders frame the risk and reward trade off.

DSV just pulled off the biggest deal in its history: the Schenker acquisition, instantly making it the world's #1 freight forwarder. That is not just a headline, it is a game-changer for pricing power, scale, and cross-selling.

According to Bejgal, that fair value estimate is built using a 6.36% discount rate and a DKK2,190 target that assumes revenue growth of 7.91% a year, earnings reaching DKK23b by 2029 and an exit P/E of 28x. Those inputs paint a picture where the recent share price implies a large gap to what this narrative expects DSV could generate if those forecasts hold.

DSV loves RFD: Logistics provider and airport hook up over air cargo
sum: Global logistics giant DSV on Saturday launched a weekly dedicated air charter service from Seoul, South Korea, to Chicago-Rockford International Airport through the end of August, underscoring the airport’s growing popularity as a cargo relief valve for crowded O’Hare airport, an hour’s drive to the east.
DSV has contracted with all-cargo airline Atlas Air to operate a Boeing 747 jumbo jet to Chicago-Rockford, continuing on to Huntsville, Alabama, and then Luxembourg, the route.

On Tuesdays, a DSV-controlled Boeing 777 from Shanghai, China, will land at Chicago-Rockford (RFD) before traveling to Incheon airport in Seoul. And on Fridays a 777 will depart Incheon and return, before heading to Jinan, China. In total, DSV is providing eight flight operations per week through RFD, primarily to support healthcare customers, said Mohamed Siraj, DSV’s vice president Air Direct / Global Gateways via email.

DSV, the third-largest logistics service provider in the world based on revenue, began utilizing RFD in November when it began weekly charter flights from Shanghai. In June, an inbound service from Luxembourg began. All the flights are operated by Atlas Air and flow through RFD on their way to other destinations in the DSV network.

“Incheon is one of Asia’s most important cargo hubs, and with this new service, DSV can provide reliable capacity and connectivity via the network we are building through Rockford,” Siraj said in a joint news release last week. “The airport has consistently demonstrated the operational reliability and flexibility needed to support scheduled international freighter services, making it a natural choice as we continue developing our air cargo operations.”

And DSV isn’t finished adding air freight service to Chicago-Rockford. The company plans to introduce a scheduled service connecting RFD to Chennai, India, later this year because of high demand from the tech sector.
The lease arrangement with Atlas Air is flexible, allowing DSV to adjust capacity and deploy aircraft where customer demand is greatest in its network.

News Piraeus declines 6% for second year, Cosco Ports results show
sum: The Californian port of Long Beach is predicted to handle more than 10m teu this ...

The Greek transhipment hub of Piraeus, controlled by China’s Cosco group, saw throughput last year drop 6%, the second consecutive year of declining volumes as the tensions in the Middle East continued to hit the eastern Mediterranean’s largest container port.

Releasing its annual results today, the partially Hong Kong-listed terminal operator said the “total throughput of Piraeus Terminal decreased 6% year on year, to 3.97m teu, primarily due to a slowdown in market demand within the Mediterranean region”.
However, analysts at Alphaliner today argued that the cause of the decline was more likely due to reshaped shipping routes since the onset of Houthi attacks on commercial shipping.

“The port of Piraeus again suffered a loss in throughput in 2025 as Red Sea service reconfigurations diverted cargo to gateways in Spain and northern Europe,” they wrote, adding that its 2024 throughput was 6.1% down on 2023.

“The port has now lost 600,000 teu in annual volume since 2023, as well as its (pre-Red Sea conflict) standing as the premier European port outside of the big three, Rotterdam, Antwerp and Hamburg,” Alphaliner said.

Meanwhile, throughput at the Suez Canal Container Terminal, of which Cosco owns 20%, grew 41% over 2024, to hit 5.5m teu, while its Kumport terminal in Istanbul/Ambarli – in which it has a 22% stake – registered 22.7% volume growth, to reach 1.54m teu, indicating continuing robustness in regional east Mediterranean demand.

European road freight rates under contract overtook spot rates in the final quarter of last year, for the first time since mid-year 2017, according to the Quarterly Road Freight Benchmark report, jointly produced by Upply, Transport Intelligence, and the IRU.

Since launching the pan-European road freight rate index at the beginning of 2017, the index base of 100, set in January that year, the only time contract rates have been more expensive than spots was in the second quarter of that year.
However, quarter four last year ended with the contract rate index at 136.9, while the spot rate level had flattened, to 135.1.
“Contract rates climbed to 136.9, a solid 2.6-point increase quarter on quarter, and a 3.1-point rise year on year.
“Meanwhile, spot rates reached 135.1, advancing modestly by 0.3 points from the previous quarter, but declining 3.3 points compared with the same period last year,” the report says.

items.t: DSV, 1164 - 2025 ANNUAL REPORT
sum: Solid financial performance in Q4 and full-year 2025, and anticipated completion of the Schenker integration in 2026
- We delivered solid financial results in Q4 2025 and reported a full-year performance for 2025 in line with guidance, despite challenging and volatile market conditions throughout the year.

- In Q4 2025, the gross profit was DKK 19,119 million and EBIT before special items came to DKK 5,592 million, driven by the integration of Schenker. The integration continues to progress fast, and we now expect to complete the integration by end-2026.

- We continued the deleveraging plan, reducing net interest-bearing debt by more than DKK 7,000 million since completion of the transaction, based on a strong adjusted free cash flow of DKK 16,335 million in 2025.
- Diluted adjusted earnings per share was DKK 50.9 per share for 2025, compared to DKK 51.6 in the previous year.
- Full-year 2026 guidance for EBIT before special items of DKK 23,000 - 25,500 million, including at least DKK 4,000 million of incremental synergies from the integration of Schenker.

Group CEO Jens H. Lund: "In 2025, we delivered a solid financial result in line with our expectations, despite significant market challenges driven by trade tensions and macroeconomic uncertainties. While supporting our customers, we progressed faster than expected on the Schenker integration, the largest and most complex integration in DSV's 50-year history. Thanks to the remarkable effort from all colleagues, we now expect to finalise the integration by the end of 2026, only 20 months after completion of the transaction. The acquisition has made DSV a new global leader in the transport and logistics industry. We have a strong position to benefit from our extensive global network and services, our commercial approach strategy and significant advancements within digitalisation and artificial intelligence. I would like to thank our customers, suppliers and all our dedicated colleagues for a tremendous effort and support."
